slides.headline: Rome Claimed Tipasa. Ruins Outlasted Empires.
slides.subheadline: Conquest built an imperial outpost. Destruction separates its ruins from modern Tipaza.
slides.svgBlueprint: Portrait viewBox 0 0 1080 1350; inherit palette throughout. Use 80px margins, Custom Brand masthead, orange kicker capsule, and 72px ink headline across three lines. Set subheadline at 30px. Place one oversized fractured-column silhouette beneath the headline. Bottom rail holds two compact date badges, issue badge, and tipaza.pub. No diagrams or callout boxes.

slides.headline: The Colony Could Not Hold
slides.subheadline: Rome’s military colony for conquering Mauretania eventually became a target itself.

items.label: Vandal destruction
items.body: The Vandals destroyed Tipasa; imperial importance had offered no guarantee of survival.

items.label: Fourth-century population
items.body: Stéphane Gsell’s population estimate reveals the urban scale behind the surviving ruins.

slides.svgBlueprint: Portrait viewBox 0 0 1080 1350; use inherited palette and 80px margins. Place headline at 58px. Render 430 CE as an 84px full-width hero, interrupted underneath by an orange fracture line. Put its body directly below. Use one lower surface panel for the 20,000 inhabitants badge at 48px and its contextual body at 28px. Keep ornament abstract, not archaeological reconstruction.

slides.kicker: THE HIDDEN BREAK / TWO URBAN STORIES
slides.headline: One Place. No Unbroken Urban Story.
slides.subheadline: Ancient Tipasa and modern Tipaza share geography, not an uninterrupted urban life.

items.label: Ancient Tipasa
items.body: A Punic trading-post became Rome’s military colony, then an important Christian hub.

items.label: Modern Tipaza
items.body: The modern town was founded after ancient destruction, reconstruction, demolition, and nineteenth-century resettlement.

slides.svgBlueprint: Portrait viewBox 0 0 1080 1350; inherited palette. Below a 58px headline, divide the content into two 440px columns separated by a 40px empty gutter. Left: broken foundation outlines and ancient-city copy. Right: restrained modern street-grid abstraction and foundation date. Do not connect the drawings. Use 48px badges, 28px bodies, and explicit multiline wrapping; preserve the written quantity three basilicas.

slides.headline: Reconstruction Met Another Conquest
slides.subheadline: Byzantine reconstruction reversed Vandal destruction, but Umayyad demolition broke the recovery.

items.label: Vandals destroy
items.body: Tipasa’s destruction breaks the Roman city’s trajectory.

items.label: Byzantines reconstruct
items.body: Reconstruction restores the city, but does not secure its future.

items.badge: the end of the seventh century
items.label: Umayyads demolish
items.body: Umayyad forces demolish Tipasa and reduce the city to ruins.

slides.svgBlueprint: Portrait viewBox 0 0 1080 1350; inherited palette and 80px margins. Set headline at 58px. Stack three milestones beside a thin vertical spine. Use orange severed segments for destruction and an ink bridge for reconstruction. Dates remain verbatim: 430 CE at 48px; relative dates at 32px with deliberate wrapping. Allocate 250px per milestone and render bodies at 28px. No invented exact reconstruction or demolition years.

slides.headline: The Ruins Sustain Their Successor
slides.subheadline: Modern Tipaza draws visitors through remains of the city that preceded it.

items.label: A new town
items.body: Modern Tipaza’s tourist importance rests principally on ancient Tipasa’s ruins—not uninterrupted urban survival.

items.label: World Heritage designation
items.body: Tipasa’s ruins received UNESCO World Heritage recognition: imperial remains became internationally recognised heritage.

slides.closingQuestion: What survives a city: its power, its people, or its remains?
